speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms you describe—tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis—are classic signs of significant respiratory distress, not a urinary tract infection. To determine the exact cause, I need to request an X-Ray of the chest and know if your mother had a fever or complications during pregnancy.

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Maternal_History

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The Chest X-Ray findings of ground-glass opacity and air bronchograms, combined with a gestational age of 32 weeks, are diagnostic for Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome. The absence of maternal fever and the presence of preterm birth further support this conclusion over sepsis or meconium aspiration.
